correctness.rationale: Exact block identities via base-four digit enumeration, uniform Cantor CDF discrepancy at most \(2^{-k}\), product perturbation at most 4·\(2^{-k}\), bounded variation at most 6 with Riemann discrepancy at most 2·\(4^{-k}\), and measure pushforward prove quantitative weak convergence. The full Cantor set is Lebesgue null, so gap-by-gap smooth changes of variables prove an absolutely continuous density. The positive \(2/y^2\) baseline integrates to 2/3 and all gaps sum to 1/3. Exact-integer and exact-rational tests cover 65,532 ratios, 1,360 unique representations and 12 stage masses; those finite tests are not used to infer infinity.

value.rationale: At the sharp \(3/2\) obstruction to bounded excess, extremal limsup alone gives no information about how frequently intermediate product ratios occur. The complete block distribution is the natural probability invariant at the construction’s four-adic scale. The result shows an unexpectedly absolutely continuous law even though the profile contains a singular Cantor staircase, decomposes its mass exactly 2/3 elementary versus 1/3 fractal, identifies a positive density over every interior value and gives an explicit effective convergence bound. This is a motivated exact structural distribution, not a small numerical improvement or a renamed known bound.
